candidate.title: SHAPE-Map
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina schematic overview of SHAPE-MaP, specifically its 1M7 probing and Mn2+-supported mutational reverse-transcription depiction. 'SHAPE-Map' is the catalogue spelling of SHAPE-MaP, not a separate version. The two RNA drawings are retained as upper and lower illustrated routes, without assigning them to named control conditions, different protocols, or separate methods. The far-left yellow/purple RNA icons accompany the label 'Selective 2′-hydroxyl acylation analyzed by primer extension and mutational profiling (SHAPE-MaP)'; no transfer arrow connects those descriptive icons to the workflow. The working routes begin with the two purple folded RNAs. Library preparation and sequencing remain a broad block. The endpoint is labeled 'Profile'; primary text explains its relationship to SHAPE reactivity. Unshown small-RNA, amplicon, randomer, in-cell, or alternative-reagent implementations are not additional extraction targets.

operations.description: The upper folded RNA gains covalent SHAPE adducts at preferentially reactive ribose 2′-hydroxyl positions. The red marks are added chemical groups; the depicted RNA topology remains the template context.

operations.label: cDNA reaction
operations.description: The upper 1M7-modified RNA is copied into cDNA under MaP reverse-transcription conditions. Polymerase reads through RNA adduct sites and can introduce non-complementary bases into the new DNA, shown as pink marks on the blue strand.
operations.mechanism: Mn2+ is the depicted cofactor promoting adduct read-through and mutational copying. The primary implementation uses SuperScript II reverse transcriptase; the schematic does not establish that any reverse transcriptase gives this behavior.
operations.information_effect: Adduct locations and relative frequencies become recoverable sequence changes in the RNA-derived cDNA. Mutation encoding is incomplete, and the RNA chemical adduct is not transferred as a covalent group onto DNA.

The terminal Profile operation captures the visible summarization interface; controls needed for corrected SHAPE reactivity are described but not drawn.
